subquestions.label: Q1(a)
subquestions.note: Same Bellivonia facts and question (define state succession, 2 pts); the answer correctly gives the VCST/VCSSPAD definition and corrects the student's answer, which confused succession with continuity.

subquestions.label: Q1(b)
subquestions.note: Faithful 4-pt card: Bellistan's view = continuity (rump state) plus secession of Livonia, Livonia's view = dismembratio, which covers both readings of the ambiguous question and fixes the student's wrong labels.

subquestions.label: Q1(c)
subquestions.note: Same question (two further criteria besides self-assessment, 2 pts); the answer lists territory, population, capital and institutions, agreement, and recognition or UN membership.

subquestions.label: Q1(d)
subquestions.note: Same dual-citizenship question (2 pts); the answer correctly applies Art 6 DADP (either state, or both jointly, against third states) and corrects the student's 'effective nationality' answer, which holds only between the two national states (Art 7).

subquestions.label: Q2(a)
subquestions.note: Same facts and question (can only states found an IO, 2 pts); the answer says IOs can also be founders (EC in the WTO, EEC/EIB in the EBRD) but private associations cannot.

subquestions.label: Q2(b)
subquestions.note: Same Red Cross question (4 pts); the answer says the ICRC is a Swiss association with partial, treaty-derived personality, not an IO, and so only a limited model.

subquestions.label: Q2(c)
subquestions.note: Same property-from-confiscation question (2 pts); the answer says the protection is treaty-based (Art 105 Charter, 1946 Convention Sections 2-4, HQ agreement) and that premises are inviolable, not extraterritorial.

subquestions.label: Q2(d)
subquestions.note: Same staff-from-arrest question (2 pts); the answer distinguishes functional immunity (Section 18(a)) from the SG's/ASGs' diplomatic immunity (Section 19) and the experts' immunity from arrest (Section 22).

subquestions.label: Q3(a)
subquestions.note: Card is labelled June 2024 and uses the same Rachastan/Antrania facts and question (8 pts); the answer covers good offices, inquiry, mediation, conciliation and UN organs, and correctly separates out binding arbitration, which the student had listed as a third-party option.

subquestions.label: Q3(b)
subquestions.note: Same question (binding procedure and its requirement, 2 pts); the card calls the rejected third-state offer 'mediation', which does not change the answer: arbitration or the ICJ, only with Antrania's consent.
